title: Allow bounded history continuity only when an entity migration is explicitly verified
scenario: A keyword was intentionally recreated during a campaign restructure. The old and new entity IDs differ, but a trusted migration record explicitly maps the predecessor to the successor. The request asks whether historical optimization evidence can inform the new entity.

predecessor_history.historical_evidence: profitable and relevant over multiple mature windows

forbidden_behaviors: Treat matching keyword text alone as sufficient proof of identity continuity.
Copy the predecessor's last known bid or serving state onto the successor as current truth.
Transfer unresolved or pending predecessor mutations as if they were applied to the successor.
Discard all predecessor evidence despite the explicit trusted migration mapping.
required_observations: A verified migration record permits bounded historical continuity between predecessor and successor.
Historical performance and mature decision evidence may be used as context, but the successor's current state must come from successor readback.
The mapping should preserve lineage without pretending the two entity IDs are literally identical.
If targeting semantics, ASIN scope, or business intent had changed, continuity should be downgraded or rejected.

rubric.requirement: Use explicit verified lineage rather than name/text similarity to carry history across a restructure.
Keep predecessor historical evidence separate from successor current-state readback.
Preserve useful mature history while clearly bounding what can and cannot transfer.
